name: Iowa

law.summary: Operators must phone the DNR field office within 24 hours of an unanticipated bypass and send a written report within 5 days. A public notice is required only when the DNR decides one is necessary; the operator then prepares it. No channel or deadline for that notice is set in the rule.

citations.title: Notification of unanticipated bypass or upset and public notices (PNs)
citations.quote: 63.6(3) Notification of unanticipated bypass or upset and public notices (PNs). In the event that a bypass or upset occurs without prior notice having been provided pursuant to 63.6(2) or as a result of mechanical failure or acts beyond the control of the owner or operator, the owner or operator of the treatment facility or collection system shall notify the department by telephone as soon as possible but not later than 24 hours after the onset or discovery. ... c. Upon notification, the department shall determine if a PN for an unanticipated bypass is necessary. If the department determines that a PN is necessary, the owner or operator of the treatment facility or the collection system shall prepare a PN.
citations.who: owner or operator of the treatment facility or collection system, when DNR so decides
citations.deadline: 24 hours to DNR by telephone; written report within 5 days; PN timing not specified

regulator_report.deadline: telephone within 24 hours to the DNR field office (after hours 515-725-8694); written report within 5 days

barriers.what: Public notice of a bypass is required only when DNR decides it is necessary; no channel is named.
Five-day written bypass reports go to DNR field offices and are not published.
barriers.note: Ask DNR for a bypass log or to join EPA SOBE.

barriers.what: Beach status by phone hotline (515-725-3434) alongside the web; bypasses reported by phone.
barriers.note: Beach data are also on the web.

readiness.rationale: No statewide overflow data: nothing in SOBE, written bypass reports are not public and the spill database rarely holds sewage. DNR press releases give dated notices for a few notable bypasses (Keokuk, August 2026) and Waterloo posts its own SSO table; both are small HTML pollers. The nine CSO cities show outfalls, the rain caution and the plain statement; check ECHO DMR for monthly CSO counts.

owner_questions: Ask Iowa DNR for a public log of bypass reports (567 IAC 63.6(3)d written submissions) or for its eRule plan?
Show DNR press releases as dated events even though they are discretionary and sparse?
Treat Des Moines' three EPA-listed open CSO outfalls as closed on the strength of 2025 press reports?
surprise: Iowa's rule makes public notice of a sewage bypass the DNR's call, not the operator's duty, and the clearest recent notice (Keokuk, August 2026) came about a week after the bypass began, through a CSO outfall just upstream of a public boat ramp.
